To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of two independent mutations in adjacent genes, in our case the adaptor protein complex 1 and the alpha 2‐macroglobulin receptor/activated in the alternative pathway 1 genes, causes a contiguous mutation syndrome in which the phenotype reflects the sum of endophenotypic traits caused by the individual gene mutations.
We identified a novel contiguous mutation syndrome in two siblings born to consanguinous parents with a combination of neurological features and early onset obesity.

We report a contiguous mutation syndrome resulting from the combined effects on phenotype of mutations in two genes 7q22 that cause the neurodevelopmental syndrome AP4 deficiency and early onset obesity, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic basis of human diseases.
the identification of the genetic cause of a complex phenotype, the characterization of a contiguous mutation syndrome, and the description of an adipokine involved in human body weight regulation.
the identification of genetic factors that contribute to the development of obesity and its comorbidities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenotype results from two independent genetic events: a founder AP4M1 c.1137 + 1G>T mutation and an independent AZGP1 c.[595A>T] variant.
our two children are the first reported cases of AP4M1/AZGP1 contiguous mutation syndrome, with the AP4M4 mutation causing AP4‐deficient syndrome and the AZP1 mutation causing obesity.
the siblings presented with a contiguous mutation syndrome resulting from mutations in AP4M and AZGP1 genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a contiguous mutation syndrome is a new genetic entity that may result from mutations in two genes in close proximity on the same chromosome.
the phenotype of the patients is due to two mutations in two genes that are close to one another.
the phenotype of our siblings results from a contiguous mutation syndrome in which mutations in both AP 4M1 and the AZGP 1 gene contribute to the phenotype of early onset obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of a genetic cause of a complex disease is not always straightforward.
high‐throughput sequencing of the exome or the whole genome in consanguineous families can reveal the genetic cause of a complex phenotype.

the clinical phenotype of patients with mutations in AP4M is more variable than previously reported and that the presence of early onset obesity should prompt the search for mutations in AZGP1 in addition to AP4M1.
